title: The AWS Free Tier Demystified 🆓
description: Exactly what you get for free for 12 months, always free, and trial services.

slides.title: Free Tier Flavours 🍦
slides.content:
# Three Types of Free

AWS Free Tier is a bundle of offers:
1. **12‑Months Free**: Services free for 12 months after sign‑up (e.g., EC2 t2.micro 750h/month).
2. **Always Free**: Services that are free forever up to a usage limit (e.g., Lambda 1M requests/month).
3. **Short‑Term Trials**: Services free from first activation for a set period (e.g., SageMaker 250 hours).

You can mix and match. The clock starts ticking from the day you create your account.

quizData.question: Which EC2 instance type is included in the 12‑Month Free Tier?

options.text: Any instance that costs less than $50

quizData.explanation: The 12‑Month Free Tier includes 750 hours/month of t2.micro or t3.micro EC2 instances (Linux/Windows). Using a larger instance will be charged.

slides.title: Key Always‑Free Services 🔓
slides.content:
# Forever Free (Within Limits)

- **AWS Lambda**: 1 million requests/month.
- **Amazon SQS**: 1 million requests.
- **Amazon DynamoDB**: 25 GB of storage.
- **Amazon CloudFront**: 1 TB data transfer out/month.
- **Amazon CodeBuild**: 100 build minutes/month.

These don’t expire after 12 months – great for learning and small projects.

slides.title: Common Free Tier Gotchas ⚠️
slides.content:
# Watch Out!

- **Data transfer out**: Only 1 GB/month free; extra costs can add up.
- **Elastic IP addresses**: Free only when attached to a running instance; unattached ones cost money.
- **Running multiple instances**: 750 hours/month total across instances – if you run two t2.micro instances 24/7, you’ll exceed the hours and be billed.
- **Storage overages**: Free Tier includes 30 GB EBS magnetic; if you choose SSD or more storage, you pay.

Always read the small print.

quizData.question: Which action might cause a charge even within Free Tier?

options.text: Running a t2.micro Linux instance 10 hours a day
Keeping an unattached Elastic IP address

quizData.explanation: Unattached Elastic IPs cost a small hourly fee. Always release them when not in use.

slides.title: Pro Tip: Use the Free Tier Usage Tracker 🧮
slides.content:
## AWS Budgets

In the Billing Dashboard, you can set up a **Free Tier Usage Alert** that warns you when you’re approaching limits. This is separate from a billing alarm (next lesson). It’s free and highly recommended.
